models.Skill: A discrete capability that an agent can invoke — e.g. web search, calendar access, or code tools. Has a category, toggle state, config fields, last-used timestamp, and a SKILL.md instructions document.
models.SkillConfig: A single configuration field for a skill — label, current value, and whether it's a secret (masked in the UI).
models.AgentSkillGroup: A grouping of skills assigned to a specific agent, used to render the agent sections in the Skills list.
models.SystemSkill: A global skill not tied to any agent — available system-wide.

relationships: Skill belongs to either an Agent (via agentId) or the system (agentId = null)
AgentSkillGroup contains many Skills for one Agent

# Shell Executor

Runs shell commands and scripts directly on the host machine.

## Actions

- `run(command)` — Execute a shell command and return stdout/stderr
- `run_script(path)` — Execute a script file by path
- `read_file(path)` — Read a file and return its contents

## Inputs

- `command` — A shell command string. Must be within `allowed_dirs` scope.
- `timeout` — Optional override for the command timeout in seconds.

## Output

Returns `{ stdout, stderr, exit_code }`. Non-zero `exit_code` should be treated as an error.

## Notes

- Commands are sandboxed to `allowed_dirs`. Attempts to access paths outside this list will be rejected.
- Do not run interactive commands (e.g. `vim`, `top`). Use non-interactive flags.
- Prefer absolute paths to avoid working directory ambiguity.

tools:

# OpenClaw Monitor

Polls the OpenClaw daemon and all registered agents for health status. Sends alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

## Actions

- `check_health()` — Returns the current health status of the daemon and all agents
- `get_unresponsive()` — Returns a list of agents that have not reported in over `check_interval × 5` seconds
- `send_alert(message)` — Sends an alert email to the configured address

## Output

`check_health()` returns `{ daemon_ok: bool, agents: [{ id, name, status, last_seen }] }`

## Notes

- This skill runs passively on a schedule — you do not need to invoke it manually.
- `send_alert` should only be called when `get_unresponsive()` returns a non-empty list to avoid alert spam.

Read, triage, draft, and send emails via the Gmail API.

- `list_inbox(max_results?)` — Fetch recent emails from the inbox
- `get_email(id)` — Fetch the full content of an email by ID
- `send_email({ to, subject, body })` — Send a new email
- `reply_email(id, body)` — Reply to an existing thread

## Inputs

## Output

`list_inbox` returns an array of `{ id, from, subject, snippet, date, labels }`.

## Notes

- Do not send emails without explicit user instruction or a clear task directive.
- Check for existing threads before sending a new email — prefer `reply_email` to keep context.

# Google Calendar

Read and write calendar events via the Google Calendar API.

## Actions

- `list_events(date_range?)` — List events in a date range (defaults to next 7 days)
- `get_event(id)` — Get full event details
- `create_event({ title, start, end, description?, attendees? })` — Create a new event
- `update_event(id, changes)` — Update an existing event
- `delete_event(id)` — Delete an event

## Inputs

- `start` / `end` — ISO 8601 datetime strings
- `attendees` — Array of email addresses
- `date_range` — `{ from: ISO, to: ISO }`

## Output

`list_events` returns `[{ id, title, start, end, attendees, location }]`.

## Notes

- Always confirm with the user before creating events with external attendees.
- Use `list_events` first to check for conflicts before scheduling.
- Events default to the `default_calendar` unless explicitly specified.

# GitHub

Interact with GitHub repositories, issues, and pull requests via the GitHub REST API.

## Actions

- `list_prs(repo?)` — List open pull requests
- `get_pr(number, repo?)` — Get PR details including diff and comments
- `review_pr(number, comments, decision)` — Submit a review with inline comments
- `list_commits(branch?, repo?)` — List recent commits
- `get_commit(sha, repo?)` — Get full diff for a commit
- `create_issue({ title, body, labels? }, repo?)` — Open a new issue
- `comment_issue(number, body, repo?)` — Add a comment to an issue

## Inputs

- `decision` — One of `"APPROVE"`, `"REQUEST_CHANGES"`, `"COMMENT"`
- `comments` — Array of `{ path, line, body }` for inline review comments
- `repo` — Defaults to `default_repo` if not specified

## Output

`get_pr` returns `{ number, title, author, diff, comments, status }`.

## Notes

- Always read the full diff before approving a PR.
- Use `REQUEST_CHANGES` if any blocking issues are found, not just `COMMENT`.
- Reference issue numbers in commit messages and PR descriptions where applicable.

# Web Browse

Fetches a URL and returns the page content as cleaned Markdown.

## Actions

- `browse(url)` — Fetch a URL and return its content
- `extract(url, selector)` — Fetch a URL and extract a specific CSS selector's content

## Inputs

- `url` — A fully qualified URL (must include `https://`)
- `selector` — Optional CSS selector to narrow extraction (e.g. `article`, `#changelog`)

## Output

Returns `{ url, title, content, fetched_at }`. Content is plain text with basic Markdown structure.

## Notes

- Some sites block automated access and will return 403. If this happens, do not retry immediately — log the failure and report it.
- Do not follow redirect chains more than 2 hops deep.
- Prefer `extract` over `browse` for large pages to reduce noise.

# Slack

Post messages and reply to threads in Slack workspaces via the Slack Bot API.

- `post_message({ channel, text, blocks? })` — Post a message to a channel or DM
- `reply_thread(channel, thread_ts, text)` — Reply to an existing thread

- Keep automated messages concise — include a summary and a link, not the full content.

# Obsidian Notes

Read and write Markdown files in a local Obsidian vault via the filesystem.

## Actions

- `read_note(path)` — Read a note by relative path within the vault
- `write_note(path, content)` — Create or overwrite a note
- `append_note(path, content)` — Append content to an existing note
- `list_notes(folder?)` — List all notes in a folder (defaults to vault root)
- `search_notes(query)` — Full-text search across the vault

## Inputs

- `path` — Relative path within the vault, e.g. `Content/Briefs/march-launch.md`
- `content` — Markdown string

## Output

`read_note` returns `{ path, content, modified_at }`.
`list_notes` returns `[{ path, title, modified_at }]`.

## Notes

- Always use `append_note` instead of `write_note` when adding to an existing document to avoid overwriting.
- Organize new notes under the appropriate folder (`Content/`, `Research/`, `Briefs/`).
- Include frontmatter (`---`) with `title`, `date`, and `tags` when creating new notes.

# OpenClaw CLI

Invokes the `openclaw` CLI binary to manage agents, apply updates, and modify daemon configuration.

## Actions

- `run(subcommand, args?)` — Run any openclaw CLI subcommand
- `get_version()` — Return the current daemon version
- `list_agents()` — List all registered agents and their status
- `restart_agent(id)` — Restart a specific agent
- `apply_update(version?)` — Pull and apply the latest (or specified) release

## Inputs

- `subcommand` — Any valid `openclaw` subcommand string
- `version` — Optional semver string, e.g. `"2.4.1"`. Omit for latest.

## Output

All actions return `{ stdout, stderr, exit_code }`. Check `exit_code === 0` for success.

## Notes

- **Only use this skill for administrative operations.** Do not invoke arbitrary subcommands without a clear task.
- Always run `get_version()` before applying an update to confirm the current baseline.
- `restart_agent` will cause a brief interruption for that agent — avoid during active task execution.
- Config changes via CLI take effect after daemon restart.

# Airtable

Read and write records in Airtable bases via the Airtable REST API.

## Actions

- `list_records(table, filter?)` — List records in a table, optionally filtered
- `get_record(table, id)` — Get a single record by ID
- `create_record(table, fields)` — Create a new record
- `update_record(table, id, fields)` — Update an existing record

## Inputs

- `table` — Table name or ID within the configured base
- `fields` — Object of field name → value pairs
- `filter` — Airtable formula string (e.g. `"{Status} = 'Active'"`)

## Output

`list_records` returns `[{ id, fields, created_time }]`.

## Notes

- This skill requires both `api_key` and `base_id` to be configured before use.
- Field names are case-sensitive and must match the Airtable table schema exactly.
- Rate limit: 5 requests/second per base. Add a 200ms delay between bulk operations.
